column3: rationale

The arm64 port establishes its original address-profile constants, topic 0015 replaces the platform split with one scalable Darwin profile, and topic 0023 retunes the auxiliary allowance so vmalloc address space stops being the binding constraint on vmapped kernel stacks.
The arm64 port owns mmap policy while topic 0015 rejects guest mappings that cross the shared sparse native hole.
The arm64 port owns its relax primitive while topic 0018 turns an interruptible Darwin spin wait into a safe cooperative IPI boundary.
The arm64 signal port owns its restorer while topic 0015 moves the trampoline with the selected guest task ceiling.
Darwin vhost-user transport support remains in topic 0010 while the generic 64-bit DMA-mask correction stays independently reviewable and droppable as topic 0014.
The shared task-layout contract remains in topic 0001 while topic 0015 selects the common scalable Darwin guest unmapped base.
The shared host-service contract remains in topic 0001 while topic 0022 adds the local IPI raise that arch_irq_work_raise() needs.
The execution core owns Linux task entry while topic 0016 adapts its first activation to fixed Darwin vCPU carriers.
The shared SKAS bootstrap owns CPU0 setup while topic 0016 installs Darwin's signal stack on the new CPU0 carrier.
The SMP core owns the IPI vector table and dispatch while topic 0022 adds the irq-work vector and its arch_irq_work_raise() implementation.
The MMU core owns guest fault dispatch while topic 0015 rejects faults that intersect the shared sparse native hole.

The execution core owns Darwin task-size setup, topic 0015 selects the common Apple task ceiling and scalable native hole, and topic 0023 caps the auxiliary allowance and gives vmalloc the whole window rather than min(window, RAM).
The Darwin host implementation owns private service declarations, topic 0016 replaces per-task scheduler hooks with fixed-carrier lifetime hooks, and topic 0017 adds the host-stop boundary.
The Darwin host implementation owns the entrypoint while topic 0017 keeps last-ditch signals from running Linux cleanup on an arbitrary carrier task.
The Darwin host implementation owns logical IRQ state while topic 0016 documents and pins its fixed-vCPU carrier ownership.

The Darwin host implementation owns fault dispatch and scheduling; topic 0015 adds shared sparse guest-range validation, topic 0016 replaces per-task pthreads with stackful task contexts, and topic 0017 stops those carriers at safe guest or idle boundaries.

The Darwin host implementation owns SMP/IPI transport, topic 0016 turns each bootstrap pthread into its vCPU's permanent named carrier, topic 0018 services cross-CPU work while a carrier waits in kernel code, topic 0019 takes the once-guard off the current-vCPU read path that Linux interrupt masking reaches, and topic 0022 publishes a self-directed vector so a local irq-work raise reaches the same cooperative drain.
The Darwin host implementation owns cooperative idle waits while topic 0017 adds the per-run stop descriptor to the wait set.
The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI declarations, topic 0015 carries the selected signal-restorer address, and topic 0017 adds the allocation-free active-stop event.
The Darwin bridge topic owns generated ABI identity while topics 0015 and 0017 advance it for the signal-restorer and host-stop contracts.
The Darwin bridge topic owns host-service declarations while topic 0017 exposes the per-run stop descriptor and predicate.
The Linux host implementation owns SMP/IPI transport while topic 0022 adds the local raise, which its queued self-directed signal already delivers correctly.
